title: Crash/retry mid-settlement: failure injected inside the approval and close transactions; crash after commit
deployment: n/a (emulator/local; binds to frozen dpl_GAmobrPxJNns8u1sHaSU2GrXVhJz code via sha)
steps: Harness 'E-crash': a Proxy over Firestore whose transaction throws on the 2nd ledger create during flush (after the reward guard + 1st ledger entry were applied to the transaction), and a variant that throws after a successful commit (response lost). Approve: inject, inspect, retry, retry again. After-commit: 20 concurrent client retries. Close: inject on the release posting, then 20 concurrent retries. HTTP: completeIdempotency made to throw once (crash after commit), retried with the same key.
observed: Run 2. Approve, failure injected on the 2nd ledger create during flush (reward guard + 1st ledger entry already applied to the tx): first attempt threw 'injected failure mid-settlement after 1 ledger write(s)…'; after it: participation 'submitted', 0 ledger entries for it, no ledgerRewards guard, tester balance 0, reconcile balanced; retry → 'approved'; 2nd retry → CONFLICT_STATE; tester credits 50 exactly, study 0. Crash after commit (response lost): participation 'approved', 20 concurrent client retries → {CONFLICT_STATE:20}, tester credits 50. Close, failure injected on the release posting: study stayed 'published', study 30, builder 0; 20 concurrent retries → {ok:1, CONFLICT_STATE:19}, closed, builder 30, study 0 (releaseEntries 2 = the 2 legs of ONE release posting: study −30 / builder +30). HTTP approve whose idempotency completion write failed: first 500 INTERNAL, retries with the same key 409 CONFLICT_STATE, 409 CONFLICT_STATE; participation approved, tester 30, 1 reward entry. Suite: 'a failed rule inside the transaction writes nothing (no guard, no entry, no participation)' ✓ 49ms; '20 concurrent top-ups of one account rerun, yet each posts exactly one balanced pair' ✓ 7475ms; crash-after-commit retries (createStudy/createFinding/topUp/moderate*) ✓ on Firestore.
notes: Hosted approve crash-after-commit: the retry with the same key re-executes the handler (failed-request-is-retryable rule) and the domain guard answers 409, unlike top-up where rule D makes re-execution a replayed 200. Invariant holds (one credit); the client sees 409 instead of a replay. Lead's call whether that is a P3 UX note. API source identical to frozen 7beaad5 (git diff 7beaad5..HEAD -- apps/api packages is empty); runs made at HEAD 6324e01..51aa93b (docs/mobile-only commits in between).
